content.text:
Complete assignment thoroughly:

# Target: crates/preloop-runner-server/src/{live_logs.rs,timeline_logs.rs,artifact_twirp.rs,cache_artifacts.rs,blob_store.rs,debug_sessions.rs,state.rs,scheduler.rs,runtime_scheduling.rs}
# Change: Read each file. Enumerate memory exhaustion via: live log ingestion, timeline logs, artifact upload/list, cache reserve, debug session events, state.rs in-memory stores (Arc<Mutex<...>>), scheduler job queues. Check for streaming vs buffering, chunk caps, per-run/session caps, total caps, backpressure.
# Acceptance: List each vector with file:line, handler, buffering mode (stream vs buffer), caps present/missing, and whether an authenticated runner can drive growth.

files.description: Unbounded per-job Vec log storage, broadcast channel without size-limiting on buffer growth, though 1024 capacity provides minimal backpressure. Vulnerable if many long-running jobs produce massive logs.
In-memory snapshotting via collect() on all timeline records. Missing total-cap enforcement. Authenticated runner can trigger frequent timeline updates to force large allocations.
Unbounded Vec growth for session events/audit trail. Missing truncation or storage-backed spilling. Authenticated runner can hammer session APIs to grow memory.
Registry maps and artifact listings are held in memory. Collecting all values into Vecs without paging. Authenticated runner can list-spam to grow memory.
Uses Vec<u8> buffers for blob processing and cache restores. Lacks streaming IO for large blob assemblies; can be driven to OOM by uploading small fragments and forcing full re-assembly into memory.
Cron history capped at 1000, but other structures (jobs/last_fires) are unbounded HashMaps. Vulnerable to schedule-spamming.

The source of truth `InnerState` is protected by a global mutex. Contains large in-memory maps (runs, artifact_v2_registry, concurrency_groups). Lacks per-run memory caps. An authenticated runner can manipulate many runs/jobs to expand these maps indefinitely.

data.summary: Enumerated memory exhaustion vectors: (1) Unbounded In-Memory Collections (`Vec`, `HashMap`, `BTreeMap`) in global state and job records; (2) Lack of streaming IO in blob/artifact operations leading to full-body buffering; (3) Lack of total-capacity enforcement for logs and audit trails, allowing authenticated runners to drive growth through high-frequency requests.
data.architecture: Memory exhaustion in Preloop is primarily driven by unbounded in-memory collection growth (`Vec`, `HashMap`) in the `InnerState` (protected by `Arc<Mutex<InnerState>>`) and per-job state. Most handlers perform full in-memory snapshots or deserialization without size-limited streams, allowing authenticated runners to trigger significant allocation spikes. Key vectors involve cron-schedule history, debug session audit trails, and artifact/cache metadata registries. Server-wide pressure is compounded by the lack of backpressure on broadcast channels and artifact-upload buffers.
